items.reason: The named half was already enforced and fixture-tested (no `${{ }}` reaches any `run:` in the tree; agent-dispatch.yml and autofix.yml already pass untrusted issue/PR text via `env:`), so I left those workflows untouched and instead closed the half the scan named as missing but nothing enforced: `check-actions.mjs` now blocks a `pull_request_target`/`workflow_run` job that checks out an event-derived ref, and blocks `${{ }}` substituted into an `actions/github-script` `script:` body.

Needs a shell: `ruff.toml`'s own stated procedure for removing the `F821` ignore is to delete the line and run `ruff check pipeline/` (ruff 0.15.0, the version CI pins) over 245 Python files, and this session has no shell and no network, so the removal could only be guessed — which the config explicitly forbids.

lessons: This repository's guard scripts are ratchets that already implement most of what a maturity scan asks for, and they document themselves in prose headers -- read scripts/security/check-actions.mjs and scripts/review/__tests__/gate-check.test.mjs before concluding a D9 gap is open, because `${{ github.event.* }}` appearing in a workflow's `env:` block is the prescribed FIX and a scanner that pattern-matches on the expression alone will report it as the bug.

Guards here are only trusted once a fixture proves they detect -- every scripts/<area>/ guard has a colocated __tests__ run by a dedicated npm script in ci.yml, and check-actions.mjs is tested from scripts/review/__tests__/gate-check.test.mjs rather than a sibling directory, so extend that file instead of adding a new test target.

ruff.toml and check-actions.mjs both encode the same house rule for debt: each exception is enumerated with why it exists and what would remove it, an exception that outlives its justification is itself a blocking finding (`stale-allowlist`), and entries may only be deleted after the verifying command has actually been run. An offline agent can add a rule to these ratchets but cannot retire an entry from one.
